draft.title: Esters and amides
card: Ester
An alcohol reacts with a carboxylic acid to form an ester and water. This is a condensation reaction, as two molecules join and lose water. The ester link is -COO-.
Hydrolysis
An ester can be split by water back into an alcohol and a carboxylic acid. This reaction is called hydrolysis, and it is the reverse of ester formation. An acid catalyst is often used.
Amide
An amine reacts with a carboxylic acid to form an amide and water. The amide link is -CONH-, where the nitrogen comes from the amine.
Both reactions join two molecules and release water. The alcohol or amine supplies the -OH or -NH group, and the carboxylic acid supplies the C=O part of the new link.
draft.remember: Alcohol + carboxylic acid gives an ester. Amine + carboxylic acid gives an amide. Each also gives water.

a.q: Ethanol reacts with propanoic acid with an acid catalyst. What are the products?
opts: An ester and water
An amide and water
An ester and hydrogen
An amide and ammonia
a.why: An alcohol and a carboxylic acid form an ester and water. An amide needs an amine, and ethanol is an alcohol with no nitrogen, so no amide can form.
a.clue: Look at what type of compound ethanol is.

b.q: Methylamine, CH3NH2, reacts with ethanoic acid. Which statement about the organic product is correct?
opts: It has a -CONH- link and water is also made
It has a -COO- link and water is also made
It has a -CONH- link and water is used up
It has a -COO- link and an alcohol is also made
b.why: An amine and a carboxylic acid form an amide, which has the -CONH- link, and water is released. The -COO- link is tempting but belongs to esters, which need an alcohol rather than an amine.
b.clue: Which functional group does the nitrogen end up in?

b.best: It has a -CONH- link and water is also made

problems.detail: "The alcohol or amine supplies the -OH or -NH group" can be read as the alcohol losing its -OH. In esterification the carboxylic acid loses the -OH and the alcohol loses only its H. The alcohol's O becomes part of the -COO- link. The line should say the alcohol supplies the O (and the amine the N) of the new link, and the acid supplies the C=O and loses -OH.

check.summary: The questions and answers are sound. One card line is misleading: it suggests the alcohol supplies the -OH lost as water, when the -OH lost comes from the carboxylic acid and the alcohol's O stays in the ester link.
